title: Authorized API and agent execution
description: Target API authority and reliability, current grounding documentation, and historical pre-reset execution/composition evidence. The reset API has an empty v1 contract; historical records and missing retired bindings do not establish current feature, identity, policy or channel execution.

intents.title: Build authorized and durable API operations before product capabilities
intents.outcome: Use canonical identity and existing data authorities to reject unauthorized work, preserve one mutation across retries and retain recoverable external intent.

journeys.title: Authenticate, scope, execute and recover a horizontal operation
journeys.situation: The runtime checkpoint exists with an empty business contract; the owner authorized the remaining horizontal identity/data/reliability foundation.
journeys.outcome: Real isolated PostgreSQL and synthetic capabilities demonstrate authenticated scoped access, durable replay/outbox control and truthful dependency failure without claiming a deployed business feature.
preconditions: Use the existing UUIDv8 account/profile and identity ledger; never treat provider subject, role selection or local data as server authority.
Apply the additive migrations only to a reviewed target; G2 runner creates its own disposable database with explicit caller acknowledgement.

existingBehavior: Database identity, Bond, receipt and effect tables and Cedar policies survived the authorized API reset.
Previous parity audit confused SQL-owned resources with missing ORM models.
invariants: Canonical UUIDv8 account remains distinct from credential/session subjects.
Missing/failed authority denies or reports unavailable; it never grants access.
Authorize before replay and lock supporting authority within the mutation transaction.
Receipt, database mutation and effect intent commit together; external send stays outside that transaction.
Keep native /api/v1 and empty business router; no compatibility aliases or fabricated ORM models.
openQuestions: Hosted identity ceremonies/project session settings, production DB login grants, proxy/container deployment and R1 require separate evidence.
Provider handlers, capability-specific reconciliation, receipt/result retention and feature/domain admission remain explicit later work.
Mobile Drizzle/PowerSync upload and offline UI paths remain rebuild work; local caches do not grant server access.

observations.title: SQL authority differs from same-named ORM model
observations.statement: Six Cedar resources now have explicit migration-backed SQL classifications; the validator preserves other model, Cedar and snapshot checks and does not certify live deployment privileges.

impacts.title: Canonical JSON fingerprints preserve prototype-named keys
impacts.statement: The reused shared sorting function now uses own-property construction so JSON __proto__ fields cannot collide through a prototype setter. Boundary validation preserves the original JSON after validation.

platformDifferences.title: Server authority is separate from local databases
platformDifferences.statement: Mobile Drizzle/PowerSync and browser data mechanisms are consumers; no client upload, feature UI, native bundle or device behavior is implemented by these server fixtures.

steps.title: Verify the acting account
steps.interaction: Verify credential claims then read the current canonical binding, account and session.

steps.title: Resolve relationships and resource facts
steps.interaction: Load a live supported Bond and server-derived target facts; use Cedar and scoped data enforcement.

steps.title: Coordinate the durable operation
steps.interaction: Reauthorize within the same transaction, reserve/lock the key and write mutation, receipt and effect intent.

steps.title: Observe replay or recoverable effect status
steps.interaction: Return committed/replayed result; explicit dispatcher fences claims and distinguishes acknowledged, failed and uncertain work.

steps.title: Receive denial, conflict or unavailable feedback
steps.interaction: Expose a safe native error/recovery classification; do not fabricate success or repeat an uncertain side effect.

transitions.action: Verify canonical identity and load supported scope.
transitions.feedback: Invalid/revoked identity fails closed; provider subject never becomes the account key.

transitions.action: Resolve resource facts and evaluate current permission.
transitions.feedback: Cross-owner/foreign-school access denies; missing policy runtime is unavailable.

transitions.action: Use the transaction/receipt/outbox boundary and recover using the same operation identity.
transitions.feedback: Matching replay returns one committed outcome; leases and DB fences bound effect attempts without promising exactly-once delivery.

transitions.action: Reject invalid, expired or revoked credentials.
transitions.feedback: Native UNAUTHORIZED or SERVICE_UNAVAILABLE; no identity/secret-bearing error disclosure.

transitions.action: Reject revoked Bond, foreign resource or unsupported scope.
transitions.feedback: Native FORBIDDEN or authority-unavailable feedback; no stored replay disclosure.

transitions.action: Detect changed payload/scope, historical incomplete work or uncertain COMMIT.
transitions.feedback: Preserve operation_key_conflict, operation_recovery_required or operation_outcome_unknown classification.

requirements.title: Verified canonical account
requirements.statement: Verify issuer/audience/algorithm/expiry and live account/credential/session bindings; transaction-bound identity/scope checks lock authority rows.

requirements.title: Scoped action and data admission
requirements.statement: Derive facts server-side, re-evaluate Cedar and enforce account RLS through transaction-local verified claims; deny unsupported scopes including principal PERSONAL.

requirements.title: Durable replay and effects
requirements.statement: Unique payload/scope-bound receipts coordinate one database mutation and outbox; reauthorize replay, fence leased work, bound retries and preserve uncertain outcomes.

requirements.title: Truthful operational admission
requirements.statement: Shared PostgreSQL account budgets, bounded pools and readiness dependency/grant/RLS checks fail closed; no application or deployment completion is inferred from an empty router.

scenarios.title: Canonical authentication and scoped isolation
scenarios.expected: Synthetic signed credentials, live isolated DB bindings, Cedar and account RLS agree on actor identity and reject cross-owner/school access.
scenarios.checkpointReason: Credential/scope admission is a checkpoint; durable mutation and effects are verified separately.

scenarios.title: Revoked or foreign scope rejection
scenarios.expected: Revocation prevents subsequent operations and stored replay disclosure; safe errors distinguish policy denial and unavailable authority.

scenarios.title: Durable execution/replay/effect recovery
scenarios.expected: Real PostgreSQL transactions exercise concurrent replay, rollback, scope conflict, leases, fenced acknowledgements, bounded retry and monotonic clock-skew behavior.

intents.title: Operate a bounded API runtime before admitting business capabilities
intents.outcome: Start, observe, cancel and drain one canonical runtime without leaking data or confusing host health with product readiness.

journeys.title: Configure, start and drain the canonical Node host
journeys.situation: The reset API has an empty native contract. Horizontal engineering is authorized; business admission remains deferred.
journeys.outcome: Valid configuration starts the bounded Node HTTP/1 host; failures stay safe, cancellation propagates and shutdown completes or force-closes by its deadline.
preconditions: Use the repository toolchain and installed SDK cohort. No business procedures or external credentials are required.

existingBehavior: Empty native contract and Hono host existed after the authorized hard reset; Node and container lifecycle paths differed.
invariants: One native /api/v1 first-party transport; no business admission.
Use the SDK procedure signal, never a stale duplicate context signal.
Health and file presence do not prove identity, policy, persistence or production readiness.
No secret-bearing exceptions in client failures or application transport diagnostics.
openQuestions: Actual edge/proxy timeout, shutdown and deployment behavior still require deployment evidence.
Identity, scoped persistence, Cedar and distributed operation/effect controls are subsequent horizontal checkpoints.

observations.title: Adapter response errors escape the Hono handler
observations.statement: Installed Node adapter response conversion/stream error paths can expose an exception; the Node boundary validates headers, sanitizes source errors and terminates failed HTTP/1 streams.

impacts.title: Production runtime is Node
impacts.statement: Docker now runs the built Node entry used by lifecycle tests; Render probes foundation readiness. External services were not deployed or changed.

platformDifferences.title: Node evidence does not certify Bun
platformDifferences.statement: Node HTTP/1 loopback is exercised. Bun remains local-only and HTTP/2, real POSIX signals and deployment proxies are not verified.

steps.title: Finish or terminate in-flight work

transitions.action: Invoke the runtime shutdown path while requests are active.
transitions.feedback: New RPC receives native 503; existing requests finish or are terminated and forced shutdown is reported.

intents.title: Understand API and agent foundations before making implementation choices
intents.outcome: Distinguish concepts, sources, adopted rules, proposed dependencies and unresolved product choices without holding the whole system in memory.

journeys.title: Read what, apply how, and preserve unresolved decisions
journeys.situation: The owner is learning API fundamentals while the reset API has no business procedures and implementation is paused for grounding.
journeys.outcome: A modular reading and source-trace path informs a bounded engineering task; unsupported choices remain explicit rather than becoming implementation claims.
preconditions: Read the current canonical domain/channel policy and identify the topic or capability under discussion.

existingBehavior: The repository has a canonical API policy, an empty v1 foundation, existing PJC and AI declarations, and historical migration records.
invariants: Research is not permission to install dependencies or resume implementation.
A protocol, framework, channel, skill and domain authority are separate responsibilities.
Documented public vendor APIs do not reveal private vendor implementation stacks.
A source observation, user rule, proposal and verified scenario must remain distinguishable.
openQuestions: The exact Anthropic announcement and intended Hermes project recalled by the owner remain unconfirmed.
Meta webhook detail pages were access/rate limited; revalidate exact selected-version behavior before implementation.
Launch channel scope, external interoperability, privacy and consequential action policies remain product decisions.

observations.title: Research and adopted implementation are different states
observations.statement: The reference bundle explains APIs, agent/channel protocols and dated primary-source examples. It does not implement bot execution, user MCP, WebMCP, AG-UI, domain operations or new framework integration in the empty foundation.

impacts.title: Bounded context packages replace full-system memorization
impacts.statement: Stable entry points, focused modules and PJC references let maintainers load a relevant topic, journey and source authorities; runtime files and dependency manifests are outside this documentation change.

platformDifferences.title: Different entry protocols share capability authority
platformDifferences.statement: Web/mobile RPC, provider webhooks, user remote MCP, browser WebMCP and developer platform MCP have distinct protocol/trust boundaries; a reference to one is not implementation of another.

steps.title: Read the relevant concepts
steps.interaction: Enter through What and load only the relevant vocabulary, channel or evidence module.

steps.title: Map concepts to actual responsibilities
steps.interaction: Use How with the canonical model and actual source contracts; identify implemented versus proposed behavior.

steps.title: Prepare the next bounded decision or task
steps.interaction: Record user rules, evidence limits and open questions without granting authority or installing a framework.

transitions.action: Follow the focused module and source links to distinguish the layer and its responsibilities.
transitions.feedback: The reader can separate a capability contract, transport, agent harness and domain rule.

transitions.action: Trace the relevant domain rule and evidence; prepare a bounded task or defer the affected product choice.
transitions.feedback: The task retains its necessary context and unresolved decisions; research claims do not become runtime assurance.

scenarios.title: Discover a modular learning and engineering path
scenarios.expected: What and How resolve their focused modules and source authorities, a PJC query finds those bindings, and unresolved choices remain visible with no claim of feature implementation.

requirements.title: Learning and engineering documentation stays granular
requirements.statement: Provide two stable What/How entry documents with focused modules, source links and PJC discoverability so the owner and agents need not retain the whole system at once.

requirements.title: Research does not imply adoption or working behavior
requirements.statement: Use dated primary sources, qualify surveys/benchmarks and ambiguous announcements, and distinguish documented vendor interfaces from private stacks. Preserve business decisions and implementation gaps; do not install or build during this grounding phase.

bindings.note: Stable educational entry point; document presence is not API feature coverage.
Implementation sequence and evidence requirements; future responsibilities are not represented as completed.
Definitions, historical choices, interaction types and RSS; primary-source learning material.
Channels, harnesses, MCP/WebMCP/AG-UI and Anthropic research; not admitted integrations.
Dated dependencies, LMS/ERP/public AI examples, interoperability standards and qualified statistics/benchmarks.
Rule authoring and decision method linking existing covenant/PJC/canonical policy, not a replacement authorization engine.

evidence.title: Documentation metadata, local references and PJC discoverability
evidence.environment: Windows host, Python/PyYAML static documentation checks and Node/tsx PJC CLI
substitutions: Static document/source inspection; no application runtime, provider or human learning assessment
evidence.limitations: Six document frontmatters and 31 local file/heading references resolve; PJC structural validation reports zero errors and trace/query commands discover the new references. Primary-source research and independent review do not establish exhaustive external correctness, future latest versions, application behavior, reader comprehension or adoption of researched frameworks. Mutable worktree evidence; no assurance-tier promotion claimed.

intents.title: Execute an authorized operation reliably
intents.outcome: Receive a scoped result or safe recovery feedback without repeating an unconfirmed mutation.

journeys.title: API admission, execution and recovery
journeys.situation: Target execution journey with historical pre-reset implementation observations and evidence below. The current reset API has no admitted business procedures or wired identity/Cedar/database/channel execution; this journey is not current working feature coverage.
journeys.outcome: A validated result or explicit rejection/recovery state.
preconditions: Verified identity and current authority for protected operations.

existingBehavior: Historical pre-reset source had a Hono identity bridge, Cedar procedures, operation receipts and AI providers. Those runtime implementations were retired; observations, bindings and evidence below retain their original historical scope and must not be read as current reset behavior.
invariants: No actor identity or school authority comes from an LLM or client hint.
Read transport cannot invoke mutations.
A retry key is not proof of server idempotency.
Evidence applies only to the named seam and substitutions.
Required authority lookup failures reject the operation instead of producing a partial principal.
Production admission uses shared rate limits; invalid configuration cannot silently select memory.
openQuestions: Real-Postgres Cedar/RLS authorization proofs still require an isolated policy-test database; the narrow receipt and bucket proof is recorded in the API guide.
Shared rate-limit tables are reachable; deployed proxy trust and cross-process contention remain unverified.
Bootstrap Cedar coverage and feature flag enforcement require procedure-specific audits.
Provider billing, retention and deployment canaries require external-system evidence.

The latest strict compiler audit reports 624 diagnostics; the API config still disables strict checks. Privacy, daily content and onboarding use native SDK inference. Legacy handler wrappers, transaction callback any types and client index-signature fallbacks remain.
Daily content caps recent lookbacks at 366 days, but pagination, full query-cost budgets, all-role authorization and real database execution remain unverified.
Ordinary reward points, badge and achievement mutations still require concurrency and idempotency verification; removing false-success catches does not make those writes atomic.

The new worktree todos router required a builder syntax correction to restore compiled startup. Its CRUD, Cedar coverage and database correctness remain unverified by liveness or the existing boundary suite.
WebSocket Node transport scenarios use real sockets with substituted identity, Cedar and database; browser authentication negotiation and actual Bun socket traffic remain unverified.

AdMob grants use one account-locked ORM transaction and explicit 503 failures. Real Postgres rollback and owner policy denial were exercised; contention, committed replay, provider delivery and historical partial-receipt reconciliation remain unverified.

MCP catalog registration caches immutable schema conversions through the SDK extension. The 2026-10-30 full host suite no longer reproduces the catalog deadlines; sustained production load remains unverified.

observations.title: Native onboarding inference and recovery classification
observations.statement: Onboarding now shares canonical schemas across native SDK implementation and Effect clients. Native errors previously lost recovery status because the client read the removed SDK status field; it now reuses the existing HTTP/code classifier. Explicit eligibility and transaction behavior remain, with live persistence and browser recovery unverified.

observations.title: Daily-content normalization previously fabricated valid results
observations.statement: The handler now uses native SDK contracts and parses unknown query results. Non-array results, invalid content types, null content and string booleans reject rather than becoming empty arrays, motivation or true. The reviewed tagged SQL calls bind values separately; scanner findings alone do not establish injection.

observations.title: Privacy success paths exposed an incomplete Cedar declaration
observations.statement: The privacy API now implements native oRPC contracts using existing canonical schemas. Success-path checks exposed an omitted Cedar appliesTo entry and invalid school attribute projection. Owner-scoped read/create policy and API projection now align; database authorization remains unverified.

observations.title: Native SDK errors are no longer patched by the test helper
observations.statement: The test client uses the installed SDK without prototype or wire mutations. Historical runs under the previous helper do not establish native v2 protocol compatibility. Current native error and batch scenarios use substituted identity and storage.

observations.title: Runtime validation does not establish compile-time contract safety
observations.statement: The converter now validates unknown declarations into native RouterContract objects without conversion casts or an application proxy. The implement wrapper still erases exact handler types through its any return. Configured compilation is not strict compilation.

impacts.title: Invalid dates and oversized recent lookbacks now reject before SQL
impacts.statement: Daily-content date inputs require ISO calendar dates and recent lookbacks are capped at 366 days as an operational request budget. Both existing route namespaces remain. Invalid stored values now produce safe errors rather than coerced content.

impacts.title: Reward callback acknowledgement requires a committed transaction
impacts.statement: Provider callbacks now return unavailable when reward persistence fails; balance reads use the existing policy client. Callers must not treat 503 as a recorded grant. Older partial receipts need reconciliation.

platformDifferences.title: Server verification and client balance reads
platformDifferences.statement: The provider-signed callback is a server ingress; browser and mobile balance consumers retain the existing JSON fields and receive explicit 503 during dependency failure. Their UI recovery behavior remains unverified.

steps.title: request
steps.interaction: Send a validated command with captured account context.

steps.title: recovery
steps.interaction: Show a safe rejection, retain the command, or reconcile its receipt.

transitions.title: Bootstrap the authenticated account
transitions.action: Validate native onboarding input, check explicit eligibility and execute existing transactional provisioning or completion settlement.
transitions.feedback: Return authoritative scope bootstrap or completion receipt; derive account identity from authenticated context.

transitions.title: Reject bootstrap or propagate failure
transitions.action: Reject unauthenticated or privileged caller-selected bootstrap, invalid completion intent or storage failure.
transitions.feedback: Return safe SDK errors and preserve HTTP/code classification through the Effect error for existing recovery callers.

transitions.title: Read validated daily content
transitions.action: Validate the date or lookback, evaluate Cedar and execute the existing parameterized read.
transitions.feedback: Return validated content with normalized driver timestamps, or the existing absent-content result for an empty query.

transitions.title: Reject invalid daily-content requests or storage results
transitions.action: Reject malformed date/lookback input before SQL or propagate malformed query results and storage exceptions.
transitions.feedback: Return BAD_REQUEST for invalid input or a safe INTERNAL_SERVER_ERROR for invalid storage, without private details or fabricated content.

transitions.title: Reject an invalid privacy operation or storage result
transitions.action: Reject invalid envelopes, other-owner or history-mutation authority, malformed stored rows and inserts without a stored result.
transitions.feedback: Return a safe native error without private storage details or false success.

transitions.title: Read or append the authenticated user's privacy ledger
transitions.action: Validate the native contract, derive the owner from authenticated context, evaluate Cedar and execute the owner-scoped SQL.
transitions.feedback: Return a schema-validated ledger or stored entry; legitimate absence remains an empty ledger.

transitions.title: Expose a dependency failure through the native protocol
transitions.action: Reject failed admission or reward storage without fabricating an empty success.
transitions.feedback: Return a safe native oRPC error with its standard code; retain private dependency details on neither the wire nor safe logs.

transitions.title: Persist a verified reward
transitions.action: Verify the signed reward and atomically record its receipt and balance increment, or acknowledge a committed replay or cap receipt.
transitions.feedback: Return a successful acknowledgement only after the ORM transaction resolves.

transitions.title: Reject unavailable reward dependencies
transitions.action: Fail verification-key lookup or persistence without acknowledging a grant.
transitions.feedback: Return 503 with safe failure details; retry using the same provider transaction ID.

scenarios.title: Verified grant, replay and quota outcomes

scenarios.title: Reward dependency failure remains unavailable

requirements.title: Daily-content reads cannot fabricate valid data
requirements.statement: Use native SDK contract inference, validate dates and the 1–366 day operational lookback budget, retain parameterized SQL and Cedar, and reject invalid stored results instead of silently coercing them.

requirements.title: Privacy ownership is independent of institutional role
requirements.statement: Use native SDK contract implementation and client inference. Preserve authenticated-owner SQL predicates and explicit Cedar read/create checks; institutional or platform roles cannot confer cross-owner access or mutate ledger history.

requirements.title: Canonical admission rejects legacy compilation
requirements.statement: The legacy compiler and its rejection tests are historical characterization, not permission to admit converted declarations. The hard-cutover target rejects legacy declaration conversion and uses native SDK contracts. Retain canonical schema identity, refinements and required validation behavior while retiring compatibility machinery.

requirements.title: MCP metadata reuse cannot reuse caller authority
requirements.statement: Reuse immutable schema conversion by identity and direction while providing a distinct caller context to each per-request SDK server. Close servers even when registration fails.

requirements.title: Dependency failures remain explicit
requirements.statement: Required storage and authority lookup failures must produce explicit unavailable feedback and safe telemetry; they must not become successful empty data or a partial principal.

existingBehavior: Historical pre-reset application proxy and eager legacy compiler behavior remains described below for context. Both the old runtime source and its legacy declaration tree were retired by the reset.

observations.title: Owner-authorized hard cutover starts with horizontal enforcement
observations.statement: The owner confirmed no deployed compatibility obligation, accepted the hybrid navigation/business ownership/channel model, and limited the current phase to horizontal foundation before feature migrations. Legacy declarations and aliases remain source debt, not accepted target behavior. Bot execution, browser WebMCP and broad user MCP exposure must not be inferred from ingress or router presence.

observations.title: Application proxy conversion has been replaced by native contract compilation
observations.statement: The compiler returns SDK contract objects with stable identities. Route fields are validated before SDK implement is invoked; source replacement requires explicit recomposition. Native contracts remain directly supported.

impacts.title: Malformed unused declarations now prevent composition
impacts.statement: Missing/invalid schemas, unsupported methods/channels, obsolete error-map fields and unsupported add_on entitlement scope now throw during composition. Existing source edits do not hot-rewrite already compiled procedures. OpenAPI uses the first declared numeric success status.

platformDifferences.title: Server composition and client authority
platformDifferences.statement: This is a server startup/composition boundary. Browser and mobile continue through their existing transports; client typing for unmigrated domains remains incomplete.
